gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in Stiftung Warentest's March 2026 test of five balcony batteries, the EcoFlow STREAM Ultra (the only one of them sold in the US) got a 'mangelhaft' grade, three of the five failed for electromagnetic interference, and Notebookcheck measured only about 90% of the STREAM's stored energy coming back out at a steady 500 W.
standout_why: I opened the three pages ChatGPT cited: californiabalconysolar.com/sb-868 (bill text only), pluginsolartracker.com California (legal summary) and KQED 2002120 (law news, a $300–2,200 price range, savings claims from the bill's backers). None names a product with a measurement, and none gives an efficiency, usable-capacity, standby or lab-grade figure for any battery. The other results are legislative PDFs and law explainers.
decides: This mostly confirms the pick and adds a caution. For a US shopper the choice is the EcoFlow STREAM Ultra (the one balcony battery sold in the US) or a portable power station plus panel. Notebookcheck got about 90% of the STREAM's stored energy out at 500 W. It got about 79% out of the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 at about 200 W, which favours the STREAM for evening home loads. Against it, Stiftung Warentest's lab failed the STREAM Ultra (4.7, mostly for electromagnetic interference, as appgefahren reports it), smartzone saw about 15 W of standby for hours, and the Anker Solarbank 3 that Warentest ranked top is not a US product. The page should present the STREAM as the plug-in pick with those caveats, and a power station as the off-grid alternative.

findings.label: Share of stored energy delivered on discharge (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: about 90% at a constant 500 W feed-in
findings.source_title: Decentralized balcony power plant system avoids 800 W limit: EcoFlow Stream in a practical test
findings.note: Measured by Marcus Schwarten of Notebookcheck; published 2025-09-23, updated 2026-10-05. Measured with a Shelly Pro 3EM meter at a steady 500 W. Notebookcheck says the figure will be lower with fluctuating loads, and that less than three quarters of the energy is usable when solar power passes through a second storage unit.

findings.label: Charging loss (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: about 15% more energy drawn at the input than stored (≈87% charging efficiency)
findings.source_title: Decentralized balcony power plant system avoids 800 W limit: EcoFlow Stream in a practical test
findings.note: Charged from the 13% discharge limit to 100%. 1/1.15 ≈ 0.87.

findings.label: Standby draw and discharge loss (smartzone.de)
findings.value: standby 'über Stunden nur 15W' (15 W for hours), with brief 30–40 W peaks during online sync; discharge losses 'rund 15%'
findings.source_title: Ecoflow Stream Ultra und Ecoflow AC Pro Speichersystem im Test
findings.note: Jonas Andre, 2025-07-21. Discharge loss measured with a smart plug. The standby reading covers the Ultra and AC Pro together. Arithmetic: 15 W × 24 h = 0.36 kWh/day, about 19% of the Ultra's 1.92 kWh rating. Combined charge and discharge loss was estimated, not measured, at about 20%.

findings.label: Stiftung Warentest balcony-battery test: line-up and overall result
findings.value: 5 units tested (Anker Solix Solarbank 3 E2700 Pro, EcoFlow Stream Ultra, FoxESS Avocado Orbit M, Growatt Nexa 2000, Zendure SolarFlow 800 Pro); grades from 'befriedigend' to 'mangelhaft'; 3 of 5 graded 'mangelhaft' for excessive electromagnetic interference; water got into the built-in sockets of 4 units in the heavy-rain test
findings.source_title: Speicher für Balkonkraftwerke im Test (Stiftung Warentest)
findings.note: Published 2026-03-19, test lead Konstantin Thurow. Rated capacities 1.92–2.69 kWh; price roughly €700–1,000. Per-product grades and measured efficiency/usable capacity are behind the paywall.

findings.product: EcoFlow STREAM Ultra / Anker SOLIX Solarbank 3 E2700 Pro
findings.label: Stiftung Warentest overall grades (as reported by appgefahren.de)
findings.value: Anker Solarbank 3 Pro: 3.3 'befriedigend' (test winner, only satisfactory grade); EcoFlow Stream Ultra: 4.7 'mangelhaft'
findings.source_title: Balkonkraftwerk-Speicher im Warentest: Nur einer ist befriedigend
findings.note: appgefahren article dated 2026-03-19, reporting the Warentest grades. On test.de the grades are locked, so they are attributed to appgefahren's report. Per appgefahren, Anker, EcoFlow and Zendure scored good or better in the 'Funktion' group (efficiency, usable capacity, reaction time).

findings.label: Usable energy and AC-charging efficiency (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 1.82 kWh drawn from the 1.92 kWh battery at a constant 400 W (≈95%); AC charging stored only 80% of input
findings.source_title: Balcony power plant system with up to 11.5 kWh and AI: Zendure SolarFlow 800 Pro review
findings.note: Marcus Schwarten, published 2025-09-01, updated 2026-10-05. Discharged to the 10% limit; AC charging at up to 1,000 W.

findings.label: Usable energy, AC charging efficiency, noise (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: about 1,600 Wh of 2,048 Wh at about 200 W (≈79%); about 1,850 Wh at 1,800 W AC (≈90%); 87% of AC charging input stored; about 35 dB at 1 m under high load
findings.source_title: 11.6 kg lighter than its predecessor: Powerstation Anker Solix C2000 Gen 2 review
findings.note: Marcus Schwarten, published 2026-02-24, updated 2026-10-05. Tested the EU version, which Notebookcheck says differs slightly from the US model. AC charging at up to 2,300 W drew almost 2,350 Wh.
